records.title: Effect of a structured exercise program on glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise is recommended for type 2 diabetes. METHODS: We randomized 180 adults to a 12-week structured exercise program or usual care. RESULTS: HbA1c decreased by 0.6 percent in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: Structured exercise improved glycemic control.
records.authors: Smith J; Doe A; Lee K

records.title: SGLT2 inhibitors and renal outcomes in diabetic kidney disease: cohort study
records.abstract: We followed 940 patients with diabetic kidney disease for 3 years. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with slower eGFR decline.

records.title: Dietary patterns and incident type 2 diabetes: a narrative review
records.abstract: This narrative review summarizes observational evidence linking dietary patterns to incident type 2 diabetes across 25 cohorts.
records.authors: Kumar R; Osei B; Novak P

Metformin versus placebo for prediabetes: a randomized controlled trial
records.abstract: In this double-blind trial, 412 adults with prediabetes received metformin or placebo for 24 months. Progression to diabetes was lower with metformin.

records.title: Barriers to insulin adherence among adults with type 2 diabetes: a qualitative study
records.abstract: Semi-structured interviews with 32 adults with type 2 diabetes identified cost, injection fear and regimen complexity as major adherence barriers.

records.title: Flash glucose monitoring and hypoglycemia awareness in type 1 diabetes
records.abstract: In a 6-month crossover study, flash glucose monitoring restored hypoglycemia awareness in 18 of 24 participants with impaired awareness.
records.authors: Novak P.; Haddad R.; Meyer U.

records.abstract: Forty-two primary care clusters were assigned to peer support or standard education. Self-management scores improved in the peer support arm at 12 months.

records.title: Bariatric surgery versus medical therapy for type 2 diabetes with obesity: 5-year outcomes
records.abstract: Among 220 patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, bariatric surgery achieved higher diabetes remission rates than medical therapy at 5 years.
